title: Commonality under Rule 23(a)(2)
summary: Commonality requires a common contention capable of producing an answer central to the claims together. A shared label, protected status, or citation to the same statute does not necessarily supply that common answer.
notes: Commonality and predominance are separate requirements. The Wal-Mart dissent objected that the majority demanded too much at the commonality stage.

sections.Meaning: Commonality requires a common contention capable of producing an answer central to the claims together. A shared label, protected status, or citation to the same statute does not necessarily supply that common answer.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the disputed contention and the proof that could resolve it across the class. Explain whether a single policy, practice, or event connects the individual claims. Use Wal-Mart’s disagreement to test the proposed connection.
